You know, Google X keeps saying that it is about dreaming big and knowing when to kill a project. But if you look at many of the projects Google X kills and the ones they embrace, it is clear that Google is still an advertising company, first and foremost and they put those initiatives ahead of any others. They want to power electronics, provide inexpensive technological solutions to getting on the internet, and provide internet access to as many people as possible to boost revenue.

Google X isn't really about creating global change, or pushing truly revolutionary technologies in agriculture, or shipping, or alternative energy, it's about protecting their core business. I think two edgy things that have risen above the chopping block is the automated car (which could change the nature of highway shipping), and their AI initiatives, which in themselves are somewhat directed at their core business as well.

Until Google stops seeing itself as an advertising company and diversifies enough that they don't have to rely so heavily on advertising revenue, they will never tackle such challenging projects as vertical farming, lighter than air transport, or solutions to third world problems.

Honestly, I was hoping that when they broke up into Alphabet that they would start focusing more on this type of shit, unfortunately, Alphabet is looking more and more like a tax shelter than anything meaningful.

What types of dogs have you found to be the most peaceful, in terms of breed/size/etc? I know there's a lot of influence from the owner, but I have a hard time imagining a passive, calm jack russell terrier, for example.

Do you have any really sweet stories? I've been having an off week, and that would really brighten it up. Thanks for doing this AMA :)

Honestly it all depends on two very important things:

A) How they are bred, and by what kind of breeder

B) How they are raised and how well they are trained

For example, Labs are the #1 breed I see, seems like most people want a chocolate, yellow or black lab. I've met some that are complete mental cases that just don't seem right in the head, but some of my favourite most relaxed dogs are labs. Every dog has a different personality.

But to get back to your question, the most peaceful dogs imo are Great Danes. These dogs are happy to sleep all day, they are extremely easy to handle at a young age and they are also very pliable in terms of training. My favourite breed is a Cattle Dog, as they have the focus and the cleverness that I like in dogs. The best first dog is a Shitzu or a Doodle, or a Mini-Doodle, they are so easy and always ready to please.

Stay away from: Boxers (again I've met great ones, but the majority is what I'm talking about), Dobermans, Rottweilers and Pitbulls. They all seem to have some real breeding issues right now that need to be addressed.

As for sweet stories I have a tonne, so if this one doesn't make you feel good I'll try the next one. We currently have a dog staying with us, a Greyhound, who has cancer in his bones. This dog was a racing dog before he was adopted out to someones home, where he has lived happily for the last year or so. However, (I'll call him Garth), Garth is currently on quite a bit of medication and is constantly in pain, so much so that he is currently on weed oil to try and help the pain. Regardless, Garth wasn't doing very good at home, always laying down, never eating, never doing anything. His mom called us up and asked if he could just stay there until his final day because she really wanted him to have a little fun and not just be stoned on the couch all day. Everyone at my work loves this dog, and while he does spend most of his day sleeping because he is ill at the end of the day, he just loves being let out for a couple hours here and there. Racing dogs are not known for their... playful demeanor... He also can't be in our "Large dog" section because they jump on him and his legs can't take the banging and crashing.

So what does Garth do in our "small dog" section? he starts ripping around and having a blast with all the little guys. He is still there everyday and has been for 2 weeks, he just seems happy everyday, he curls up on the couch and races in to the small dog section when he is called. He is a very sweet dog and I'll be very sad when he goes, but at least for now he is having a fucking blast.

I'm not a groomer so I'm not sure if I'm answering your question right but... We always reserve the right to reject a dog from our facility, overly aggressive dogs or dogs that show consistent intent to harm, or even dogs that bite us, tend to be banned from the daycare. That is a last straw kind of thing though, we will always try and work with the animal first. In the daycare putting them on a noose and walking with them helps, giving dogs consistent alone time and trying your damndest to have fun with them generally helps dogs accept integration in to the so called "pack". As for the grooming side of things they tend to work pretty hard, some dogs buck and kick around in the tub, and then when they are being tried off, they bite when you do their nails and cry when you clean their ears. It is a very tough job imo and people don't really appreciate the patience dog groomers exhibit on a daily basis.

If a dog is being mis-treated we always ask the owner first, it is pretty easy to gauge if they're totally lying. For example we once had a very thin dog, extremely thin, we were all worried and even fed her more than we were supposed to when she stayed overnight. It was a growing puppy and it just didn't look right. The owner absolutely knew of the issue when we asked and the dog filled out when it grew older, it was just a hungry pup I guess.

Then there are the true fuckups, the people that own dogs that don't even want to go home after their stay. I remember one dog in particular that literally would run from its owners and try to go back in to the daycare, the dog was so sweet but also had some behavior issues with other dogs that needed to be worked on. We ended up convincing the owners to re-home the dog because they simply did not understand dog ownership, they agreed and the dog is living happily ever after.

I wouldn't say shaping a dogs hair is common at all, nor popular. I do however see one or two dogs a month get a wild groom. My favourite is the lion cut when done properly it is an extremely cool look for a dog.
